newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends day firmer on Iraq news, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends day firmer on Iraq news, NYMEX.

text.p: IPE June Brent crude ended the day over 40 cents firmer on the back of strong NYMEX WTI crude and products markets and on concern over Iraqi helicopters breaking a 'no-fly' zone imposed by the U.S. and other Western powers.
May WTI crude and prompt unleaded gasoline on the NYMEX were Monday's market leaders brokers said but they added a note of caution on the relatively thin volumes traded on the IPE.

June Brent on the IPE ended Monday up 42 cents at $18.34, down from the day's high of $18.48 a barrel. The contract traded just under 22,400 lots and brokers said this should have been closer to 30-35,000 lots for some analysts to see it as a solid break upwards.
'The other thing is the expiry on (May) WTI - we could see the bottom of the range again once that support goes,' one commented.
The May WTI contract expires on Tuesday and short-covering on the prompt contract on Monday supported prices.
NYMEX gasoline gained substantial ground on Monday, closing at 62.70 cents a gallon, up from a 61.25 cent a gallon open.
U.S. spot refined traders said the markets would keep a close eye on gasoline production across the country this week as the widely awaited peak summer demand season inches closer.
Iraq said on Monday that it was sending helicopters to pick up Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border. The White House urged Iraq to reconsider its decision, and said it would 'respond appropriately'.

'So maybe they are going to lose some of their oil is what the market is thinking,' one broker said refering to a U.N. accord which allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months on a renewable basis in order to buy food.
IPE May gas oil closed earlier up $2 at $165.50 a tonne and was called unchanged based on the Brent and NYMEX closing prices.
